therapeutics_text: > RHEUM. Is another remedy which like Jalapa , has been abused by the old school, but is very valuable when used homopathically. The leading indication is sour stools . They may be brown mixed with mucus, or thin and pasty. There is often much pain before the stool , of a colicky nature, and there may be tenesmus after stool. It is most useful in colicky diarrha of children. There is another very characteristic symptom, viz.,: "Not only the stools are sour; the whole child smells sour , no matter how much it is bathed." In colic and diarrha during dentition a choice will sometimes have to be made between this remedy and Magnesia carb .
